Good morning church, you may be seated.
Turn to your neighbour and say neighbour, you look blessed today.
Let us open our Bibles to First Corinthians chapter thirteen.
Today I want to talk to you about the love that never fails.
#SHOW 46 13 4 7 Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up
Love is patient, love is kind, it does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
Now notice that Paul does not describe love as a feeling, he describes love as a way of acting toward people.
Many of us think love is something we fall into, but the Bible shows that love is something we choose every day.
The point is this: love is patient when people are slow, and love is kind when people do not deserve kindness.
When your husband forgets your birthday again, patience is love in work clothes.
When your colleague takes the credit for your work, kindness is love refusing to keep a record of wrongs.
Can I get an amen?
Amen.
Paul was writing to a church that was full of gifts but empty of love.
They spoke in tongues, they prophesied, they had knowledge, but they were proud and divided.
And Paul says if I have all these gifts but have not love, I am nothing.
Remember that gifts without love make noise, but love without gifts still makes a difference.
#SHOW 46 13 8 8 Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail
Love never fails.
Prophecies will cease, tongues will be stilled, knowledge will pass away, but love remains.
The reason love never fails is that love comes from God, and God never fails.
You cannot produce this kind of love by trying harder, you receive it from the God who first loved you.
First John tells us that we love because he first loved us.
So the secret of loving difficult people is to stay close to the God who loves difficult people, including you and me.
I remember a woman in our church who cared for her sick mother for eleven years without complaining.
When I asked her how she did it, she said, Pastor, every morning I ask God to fill my heart with his love before I fill her cup with tea.
That is what this means: love is not a mood you wait for, it is a gift you receive and then give away.
Some of you are tired of loving people who do not love you back.
I want you to know that the love of God does not run out, even when your strength runs out.
Number one, receive the love of God for yourself before you try to give it to others.
Number two, choose to act in love even when you do not feel loving, because feelings follow obedience.
Number three, keep no record of wrongs, forgive quickly and let God handle what you cannot fix.
Somebody say forgive quickly.
Forgive quickly.
Forgiveness is love that refuses to let yesterday's hurt control today's choices.
When you hold on to bitterness, you build a prison and then live inside it yourself.
But when you forgive, you set a prisoner free and discover the prisoner was you.
#SHOW 45 5 8 8 But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
God demonstrates his own love toward us in that while we were still sinners Christ died for us.
God did not wait for us to become lovable before he loved us, and that is the standard for our love too.
In conclusion, love is patient, love is kind, love forgives, and love never fails because God never fails.
This week, choose one person who is hard to love and show them one practical act of kindness.
Let us pray.
Father, fill our hearts with your love so that we can love others the way you have loved us.
In Jesus' name, amen.
